correctness.rationale: The full primary text proves that \(\mathcal S_W(u,v)=(W^{1/2}u,W^{1/2}v)\) maps the compatible cone bijectively onto itself and satisfies \(\mathcal S_WT_W=T_I\mathcal S_W\). Defining \(\|z\|_{W,\times}=\|\mathcal S_Wz\|_\times\) makes this conjugacy an exact isometry. Therefore every corresponding \(k\)-step gain ratio is equal, and the cone bijection makes the suprema exactly equal. The contraction-horizon and best-prefactor statements are direct functions of this common gain sequence. The realization lemma confirms that all compatible states used by the supremum are algorithmic states.

originality.rationale: The primary paper states equality only of the asymptotic homogeneous growth radius and, in the Euclidean product norm, records a condition-number finite-horizon sandwich. The companion Lyapunov paper supplies a common one-step Lyapunov law, while the earlier sharp-rate paper supplies a common optimal asymptotic threshold. Neither inspected paper states exact equality of the complete finite-horizon worst-case gain sequence in matched norms or the resulting exact contraction-horizon and prefactor profiles. Targeted published-research searches found no statement-equivalent result.
residual_risks: Exact gain preservation under a conjugacy made isometric by a pulled-back norm is a general linear-algebra principle and may be stated abstractly in dynamical-systems literature; the optimization-specific finite-horizon consequence for this newly introduced compatible BB cone was not found.
The matched norms differ across weights, so the theorem does not imply identical transients under one common physical or Euclidean metric.
A later version of the primary preprint could explicitly add this observation; the originality comparison is to the inspected public versions.

value.rationale: The primary paper builds its global \(R\)-linear theorem from a finite-step contraction principle, so the finite-horizon gain sequence is a central dynamical object rather than an arbitrary statistic. Exact equality of \(A_k\) for all \(k\) shows that spectral weighting changes coordinates but not the sharp transient profile once the metric is transported with the conjugacy. This identifies the exact contraction horizon and exact best rate prefactor for BB2 and every fixed spectral-weight rule from BB1 without a condition-number loss, while clearly separating this metric-invariant fact from Euclidean transient behavior.
